title: Broken tests triage
description: Live CI failures over the last 2 days, grouped into distinct failures (by failing test id + a normalized error signature) and classified by how each is behaving right now, most urgent first. Reach for this to answer "what CI failures should I care about right now": it is the triage counterpart to the test-health queue (which ranks week-long unreliability). Each row's state is the verdict: breaking_master (failing on the default branch and that job's latest run is still red, so trunk is broken now), blocking_merge_queue (failing only on merge-queue gate branches, so it stopped a merge on a commit that had already passed the PR's own CI: the conflict-with-trunk class the queue exists to catch), novel_burst (first seen within a day and already spreading across branches, not on trunk yet), potentially_resolved (hit trunk but that job is green again), flaky (sporadic across two or more branches over more than a day), or pr_only (confined to one branch: one PR's own problem). Also returns breaking_master_jobs, the default-branch jobs whose latest run is red. Pass a row's latest_run_id and latest_ci_engine to run-failure-logs to read the failing lines. Caveats: fingerprinting is pytest-only for now (jest/playwright/cargo failures aren't grouped yet), and the breaking/resolved distinction needs the job-level source synced: without it those failures fall through to flaky/pr_only rather than being misreported. Counts are absolute, never rates (passing runs aren't in this data).

methodDocumentation.text: The broken-tests triage panel: live CI failures over the last 2 days grouped into distinct failures (by test id + normalized error signature) and classified by how each is behaving right now: breaking trunk, blocking the merge queue, a new failure spreading across branches, probably-resolved, flaky, or one PR's own problem: ranked with the most urgent first. A blocking_merge_queue row is a failure on a merge-queue gate branch that never hit trunk: the commit had already passed the PR's own CI, so it is the semantic conflict the queue exists to catch, and it is holding up landings. Also returns breaking_master_jobs, the default-branch jobs whose latest run is red. Reach for this to answer 'what CI failures should I care about right now'; expand a row's latest_run_id via run_failure_logs for the failing lines. Fingerprinting is pytest-only for now (jest/playwright/cargo failures aren't grouped yet), and the breaking/resolved distinction needs the job-level source synced: without it those failures fall through to flaky/pr_only rather than being misreported.

* `blocking_merge_queue` - Blocking Merge Queue
* `novel_burst` - Novel Burst

* `pr_only` - PR Only
